content.value_statement: Metabolic modeling workflows require precise COBRApy patterns for setup, optimization, and validation. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through FBA, FVA, knockouts, media design, and SBML model handling.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to load and save COBRA models in SBML, JSON, YAML, and MATLAB formats.
Provides usage patterns for FBA, pFBA, geometric FBA, and flux variability analysis.
Guides single and double gene or reaction deletion studies.
Explains growth media, minimal media, and production envelope analysis.
Includes workflows for flux sampling, strain design, model validation, and debugging.
limitations: Requires users to install COBRApy and compatible optimization solvers separately.
Examples use sample model identifiers and must be adapted to local model files.
Does not verify biological conclusions or model curation quality.
Does not provide executable package code or an automated test suite.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Growth Simulation
use_cases.description: Load a metabolic model, set the medium, run FBA, and interpret growth results.

use_cases.title: Screen Gene Knockouts
use_cases.description: Plan single or double deletion studies and classify essential genes by growth impact.

use_cases.title: Validate a Draft Model
use_cases.description: Check feasibility, blocked reactions, mass balance, duplicate reactions, and orphan genes.

prompt_templates.title: Load and Optimize a Model
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for a standard COBRApy model.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me load a COBRApy model, run flux balance analysis, and explain the objective value and solution status.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Growth Media
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for testing nutrient conditions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a COBRApy workflow to compare aerobic and anaerobic media and report growth changes across conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Knockout Screen
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for gene essentiality analysis.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a COBRApy analysis plan for single gene deletions, essential gene detection, and result export for review.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Production Strain
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for metabolic engineering analysis.
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through production envelope analysis, growth constraints, beneficial knockout screening, and validation for a target metabolite.

output_examples.input: Load a model and run FBA.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step plan that loads the model, checks solver status, reports growth rate, and reviews active fluxes.

output_examples.input: Find essential genes in an E. coli model.
output_examples.output: A knockout workflow that defines a growth threshold, classifies genes by impact, and recommends result tables.
A validation checklist covering medium constraints, blocked reactions, mass balance, dead-end metabolites, and loopless FVA.

best_practices: Use context managers for temporary model changes so baseline models remain unchanged.
Check solution status and feasibility before interpreting flux values.
Prefer SBML for model exchange and record solver settings with each analysis.
anti_patterns: Do not interpret flux results before confirming the optimization status is optimal.
Do not mutate growth media without assigning the updated medium back to the model.
Do not treat sample model identifiers as substitutes for curated project models.

faq.question: What is COBRApy used for?
faq.answer: COBRApy supports constraint-based analysis of metabolic models, including growth prediction, knockouts, media design, and flux analysis.

faq.question: Does this skill install COBRApy?
faq.answer: No. It explains COBRApy workflows. Users must install COBRApy and any required solvers separately.

faq.question: Can it work with SBML models?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes patterns for reading and writing SBML models with COBRApy.

faq.question: Does it support gene knockout studies?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers single and double gene or reaction deletion workflows and essentiality analysis.

faq.question: Can it validate metabolic models?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes checks for feasibility, blocked reactions, mass balance, duplicate reactions, and orphan genes.

faq.question: Is biological interpretation guaranteed?
faq.answer: No. Results depend on model quality, solver settings, constraints, and domain review.
